evals.prompt: I have a Flutter BLoC that subscribes to a stream from a repository in its constructor. The stream keeps a database connection alive. How do I correctly subscribe to the stream inside a BLoC and make sure it gets cancelled when the BLoC is closed?
evals.expected_output: Shows two patterns: (1) emit.forEach — preferred, auto-cancels when BLoC closes, no manual subscription needed; (2) StreamSubscription with late field, cancel in close() override calling super.close(). Explains why emit.forEach is preferred. Notes no rxdart, native Dart streams only.

evals.prompt: My Flutter app's search screen fires an API request on every keystroke. I need to debounce it so the request only fires when the user stops typing for 300ms. I'm using BLoC. What's the correct pattern — I don't want to use rxdart.
evals.expected_output: Shows restartable() transformer from bloc_concurrency on the SearchQueryChanged event + Future.delayed inside the handler. Code: on<SearchQueryChanged>(_onSearch, transformer: restartable()); inside handler: await Future<void>.delayed(Duration(milliseconds: 300)); then fire request. Explains why restartable() cancels the previous handler including the delay. Explicitly states no rxdart needed.

evals.prompt: What are the most common async anti-patterns in Dart/Flutter that I should avoid? My team is doing a code review and I want to know what to look for.
evals.expected_output: Covers all 6 anti-patterns from the skill: fire-and-forget (no await in business logic), swallowed exceptions (empty catch), uncancelled subscriptions (memory leak), dynamic async types (Future<dynamic>), rxdart usage (FORBIDDEN), and compute() legacy usage (use Isolate.run() instead). Each with bad/good code examples.
